text: If an AI quietly took over your scheduling, shopping, and messaging for a month, you'd miss the convenience more than the freedom.

brief.title: Delegated Life
brief.plain_english: This asks whether convenience becomes so persuasive that giving up small pieces of personal agency starts to feel normal.
brief.background: Many people already let algorithms shape what they watch, buy, and respond to. This question pushes that pattern one step further: if an assistant became eerily good at running your day, would you still care that it was steering it?

key_terms.definition: Your felt sense of directing your own choices.
How gradual convenience makes surrendering control feel harmless.

text: A decade from now, which AI future would you rather live inside?
options: A few tightly regulated frontier labs
A slower world with strict limits on deployment

brief.title: Who Gets the Keys?
brief.plain_english: This asks which tradeoff feels safest and most human: openness, concentration, public stewardship, or restraint.
brief.background: AI is becoming less of a tool and more of an operating layer for society. The real choice may not be whether it advances, but who gets to shape the rules, speed, and access.

answer_insights.insight: Innovation spreads fast, but so does misuse.

answer_insights.answer: A few tightly regulated frontier labs
answer_insights.insight: Control may improve safety, but it concentrates power.
Shared oversight could matter more than raw speed.

answer_insights.answer: A slower world with strict limits on deployment
answer_insights.insight: Progress is tempered in favor of social breathing room.

text: Rank these by how much they distort democracy before election day even arrives:

brief.title: Democracy Before the Ballot
brief.plain_english: This asks what does the most damage before people even get to cast a vote.
brief.background: Political outcomes are shaped long before election day. Attention systems, cynicism, money, and fractured media all change the environment people make decisions inside.

answer_insights.insight: The emotional tempo of politics gets engineered upward.
Agenda-setting can be bought before the public notices.
People stop sharing the same reality long before they disagree on policy.
When people feel drained, manipulation barely needs to try.

text: The most expensive thing in your life is not what you buy - it's what your attention gets trained to want.

brief.title: The Price of Attention
brief.plain_english: This asks whether the real cost of modern consumer life is desire itself, not just spending.
brief.background: Many purchases are downstream of attention patterns. If systems continually shape what feels urgent, tasteful, aspirational, or missing, then desire may be the product long before the product is sold.

text: When a close friendship starts drifting, what matters most to you?
options: A memorable shared experience that resets the bond

brief.title: Saving the Drift
brief.plain_english: This asks what kind of repair matters most when closeness fades slowly instead of ending dramatically.
brief.background: Most friendships don't break; they thin out. The question is whether connection is rebuilt through words, rhythm, generosity, or moments strong enough to alter momentum.

answer_insights.insight: Clarity matters more than guessing.
Trust is rebuilt through steady signals, not intensity.
Care can survive even when timing doesn't.

answer_insights.answer: A memorable shared experience that resets the bond
answer_insights.insight: Sometimes presence succeeds where analysis fails.

text: Rank these by how accurately they predict how someone will handle real pressure:

brief.title: Pressure Reveals Character
brief.plain_english: This asks which trait tells you the most about how a person behaves when life stops being easy.
brief.background: People often look impressive in calm seasons. Pressure exposes different strengths: steadiness, discipline, flexibility, or the ability to stay human when things get hard.

answer_insights.insight: Staying steady may matter before every other skill can function.
The person who shows up under strain often shapes the whole outcome.
Adaptability can outperform brute confidence when conditions change.
Lightness can be a serious form of resilience.

text: A trip is more transformative when it confuses you a little.

brief.title: Useful Disorientation
brief.plain_english: This asks whether the best travel stretches you precisely because it doesn't fit your habits right away.
brief.background: Some trips restore us. Others rewire us. Being slightly lost, mismatched, or culturally off-balance can shake loose assumptions that comfort never touches.

text: You're starting something new tonight. What matters most?
options: A world you can disappear into
The thing everyone is talking about

brief.title: What Actually Hooks You
brief.plain_english: This asks what pulls you into a new story before you know whether it deserves your time.
brief.background: We often say we want originality or quality, but attention is usually captured by a more specific magnet: atmosphere, people, ideas, or social gravity.

answer_insights.answer: A world you can disappear into
answer_insights.insight: Immersion matters more than plot efficiency.
Attachment to people beats attachment to premise.
The best entertainment earns mental afterlife.

answer_insights.answer: The thing everyone is talking about
answer_insights.insight: Shared cultural timing can be its own kind of value.

text: Rank these by how much they upgrade an ordinary night out:
options: A first sip that sets the mood

brief.title: The Hidden MVP of a Night Out
brief.plain_english: This asks what most transforms a meal from merely decent into memorable.
brief.background: A great night out is rarely about one expensive centerpiece. Tiny sensory details often determine whether the evening feels generic, intimate, celebratory, or unforgettable.

answer_insights.insight: Warm abundance changes the mood before the meal begins.
Atmosphere can outperform ingredients in memory.

answer_insights.answer: A first sip that sets the mood
answer_insights.insight: The opening note often defines the entire evening.
A strong ending can rewrite the story of the night.

text: Most people don't need more health information - they need a life that makes healthy choices easier.

brief.title: Healthy by Design
brief.plain_english: This asks whether behavior change is mostly a knowledge problem or mostly a systems problem.
brief.background: Many people already know what would help: sleep, movement, better food, less stress. The harder question is whether their environment, schedule, cost of living, and social rhythm make those choices realistic.

text: Which small ritual most improves the quality of your week?

brief.title: Tiny Rituals, Big Difference
brief.plain_english: This asks which small repeated act has the biggest effect on your felt quality of life.
brief.background: People often overestimate dramatic resets and underestimate rituals. Tiny practices can quietly determine energy, mood, self-trust, and the texture of an entire week.

answer_insights.insight: Stillness creates room before the world starts making demands.
Momentum in the morning can reshape the whole day.
Creation can restore agency in a consumption-heavy life.
Order tonight often becomes calm tomorrow.

text: Rank these by how often they genuinely wake people up:

brief.title: What Wakes a Human Being Up
brief.plain_english: This asks which force most often snaps people out of autopilot and into deeper awareness.
brief.background: Spiritual change rarely happens through abstract ideas alone. It often arrives through pain, awe, stillness, or being asked to carry something real.

answer_insights.insight: Loss can strip away illusion with brutal speed.
Wonder can re-order attention without force.
What finally becomes audible may be what was always there.
Being needed can mature a person faster than being inspired.

text: If you had to remove one feature from online shopping forever, which would improve life most?

brief.title: What Makes Buying Hard to Resist
brief.plain_english: This asks which common e-commerce feature most intensifies impulse, frictionless desire, or decision fatigue.
brief.background: Online shopping isn't just inventory plus payment. It's a behavioral architecture designed to keep wanting frictionless and reflection delayed.

answer_insights.insight: The shorter the pause, the weaker reflection becomes.
Desire becomes harder to separate from targeting.
Decision paralysis can masquerade as informed choice.
Lingering desire keeps asking for a future self to justify it.

text: A society becomes fragile the moment every disagreement is treated like a moral emergency.

brief.title: Permanent Emergency Culture
brief.plain_english: This asks whether moral intensity eventually weakens a society's ability to think, persuade, and coexist.
brief.background: When every conflict gets framed as ultimate, people lose the space to distinguish danger from difference. That can turn politics into a constant state of escalation.

text: Rank these by how likely they are to change human identity first:
options: Synthetic voices that sound exactly like us

brief.title: The First Identity Shift
brief.plain_english: This asks which emerging technology is most likely to alter how people experience being a self.
brief.background: Not all technological change is economic or practical. Some tools reshape intimacy, memory, perception, and selfhood itself long before institutions catch up.

answer_insights.insight: Relationships may be the fastest route into identity change.
The boundary between thought and interface gets thinner.
When perception is layered, reality becomes co-authored.

answer_insights.answer: Synthetic voices that sound exactly like us
answer_insights.insight: Identity shifts when presence can be reproduced without the person.
